summary.text: 奶 commonly means “milk” and is also recorded for “breast” and “nursing.” Its usual analysis pairs 女, associated with women, with 乃 as a proposed sound element. Both are now read nǎi in Mandarin, but that match does not prove an ancient sound link.

formation.text: The usual dictionary analysis is phonosemantic: 女 contributes a woman-related meaning, while 乃 is assigned a phonetic role. A competing late account proposes that a graph said to mean “milk” was mistaken for 乃 and combined with 女; the graph, its reading, and its connection to 奶 have not been independently verified.

components.text: 女 contributes a woman-related meaning in the usual analysis. No distinct earlier form or graphic change for this component within 奶 is documented here.

乃 is assigned the phonetic role in the usual analysis. The proposed confusion with an alleged older graph for “milk” concerns the history of the whole character; it does not establish a substitution within this component.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin pair is nǎi : nǎi. The local Baxter–Sagart data list two possible entries for 乃, *nˤə(ŋ)ʔ and *nˤəʔ, but no entry for 奶, so they provide no system-matched historical pair. Reported Zhengzhang values for both characters are not independently validated here.

sound.text: Both characters have the modern Mandarin reading nǎi; this contemporary match alone does not establish their historical relationship.

history.text: 奶 is not recorded in 說文. A later conjecture reports a bronze graph said to be pronounced 乃 and to mean “milk”; it proposes that the graph was confused with 乃 and 女 was added. The alleged graph, its reading, and its connection to 奶 have not been verified, so this does not establish 奶’s graphic history.
The cited references to oracle-bone and bronze forms are unpublished, and the inspected chart does not include 奶. No ancient or early printed form is verified here.

uncertainties.text: Dictionaries give the 女 + 乃 analysis, but the supplied historical sound comparisons do not independently confirm 乃’s phonetic role.
The cited uses establish neither the earliest attestation nor the chronology connecting breast, milk, nursing, and infant-related meanings.

senses.text: “Breast” is a recorded sense, with a cited literary example; the material here does not date its earliest use.
奶 is recorded for “milk,” including in 牛奶. The cited literary example is undated here, so it does not show when this use began.
Nursing is a recorded use with a cited literary example. Its date and chronology relative to the breast and milk senses are unresolved.
Modern dictionary records include the sense “milk”; the supplied readings include Mandarin nǎi.

limitations.text: The cited sources attest several uses but do not establish their chronology or semantic transitions. The late proposal about an earlier graph for “milk” concerns graphic history, not a demonstrated change in meaning.
